webpage.text:
Spain slingshot ride accident: Cable snaps midair at Seville fair injuring four

Cable snaps midair on thrill ride, sending panic through crowded festival


By

 * Kaylee Remington, cleveland.com

SEVILLE, Spain — A malfunction on a slingshot-style amusement ride at a popular spring festival in southern Spain sent riders crashing and left people injured.

The incident happened Friday at the annual Feria de Abril in Seville when a cable on the “Steel Max” ride snapped during operation, causing the capsule carrying riders to swing violently and strike part of the structure.

Emergency services said four people were injured, including two children who were on the ride and later taken to a medical center. Two others on the ground were hurt by debris. Authorities described the injuries as minor.

The Seville Emergency Service Department said in a public statement that responders quickly secured the area, treated the injured at the scene and took the riders for further evaluation, noting a “rapid intervention of all emergency services.”

Witness video showed the capsule being launched high into the air before the cable failure caused it to drop and slam into a support structure, prompting screams and panic among bystanders.

Firefighters shut down the attraction immediately after the incident, while local police inspected safety documentation and Spain’s National Police opened an investigation into what caused the failure.

The Feria de Abril, a weeklong event that draws crowds each year with rides, food and cultural festivities, continued as authorities worked to determine whether mechanical issues or other factors led to the incident.

Fundraiser for Jarrod Male by Jill Young : A New Pet Ambulance for the region

ONE of the Pet Ambulances died.

The pets of Canberra and surrounds rely on    the TWO ambulances to transfer sick animals between the vet clinics and overnight


emergency hospitals.

People  without transport or close family and friends contact Jarrod and Claudia to help get their sick family members to appointments and home again. They also donate their time in helping transport the Pets in the Park to the vets on surgery day

The Pet Ambulance operates 24/7, 365 days a year 

Canberra, its time to show your support and help get a second Ambulance so our pets don’t suffer.

Jarrod and Claudie would not ask for your help but I will!!

Please help by donating whatever you can and show Jarrod and Claudie how much we appreciate and need their service.
